speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to determine the cause, have you noticed if these lesions are painful or if you have a fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome. The patient's recent initiation of captopril and discontinuation of meloxicam, combined with blistering on the forearm and painful oral/ genital ulcers, strongly suggests a severe cutaneous adverse reaction. While hiking and poison ivy were mentioned, the temporal relationship with new medications and the specific nature of the mucosal involvement makes SJS the primary concern. Please confirm if you have experienced any flu-like symptoms (fever, cough, sore throat) in the week prior to the rash onset.
